headline: Highest risk is data leakage: dbt-core can reach warehouse data while dagster has no filesystem/network surfaces, so most pairwise harms are limited but compliance and cascading misuse remain possible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default injection bridge is documented. dagster has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem read/write, or MCP surfaces, and dbt-core exposes only allowlisted network egress plus warehouse API calls. Without a shared channel, dbt-core output cannot directly hijack dagster, and dagster cannot ingest it by default.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies dbt-core output into dagster prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF either agent is wrapped with a shared message queue or clipboard bridge, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected except through explicit human review.
Disable any automation that copies model output into downstream prompts.
Use separate workspaces and no shared clipboard.
Log and inspect any manual handoff text before reuse.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches warehouse data and can send it to a warehouse API, while dagster is a data-engineering orchestrator with no local filesystem or network egress surfaces shown. The pair can still leak sensitive warehouse data through dbt-core outputs or logs into dagster-managed workflows in default analytics setups, so the pathway exists even though dagster itself is constrained.
conditions: IF dbt-core renders warehouse-derived values into artifacts that dagster stores or forwards, leakage occurs.
IF dagster is configured to capture stdout/logs from dbt runs, sensitive data can propagate.
mitigations: Redact warehouse values before passing artifacts onward.
Turn off verbose logging for dbt runs.
Store outputs in a restricted location with short retention.
Review any dagster asset materializations for sensitive fields.
requires-engineering: add automated secret/PII scanning on pipeline outputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A write-write conflict is not evidenced: dagster has no write_filesystem or modify_git_state capability, and dbt-core only shows allowlisted network egress plus warehouse API access. The pair can still contend over shared warehouse resources, but the rubric’s high-severity filesystem/git conflict is not present.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same warehouse objects, mutable-resource conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator adds shared filesystem writes for either agent, the conflict profile changes.
mitigations: Assign separate warehouse schemas or roles.
Serialize writes to shared tables.
Use read-only access for dagster where possible.
Add a simple lock or lease around shared jobs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can produce warehouse-facing transformations that dagster may consume as pipeline inputs, but dagster is not documented here as critically evaluating those outputs. That creates a default path where one agent’s output becomes the other’s input without verification, which can cascade bad assumptions into downstream analytics work.
conditions: IF dagster uses dbt artifacts or logs as authoritative inputs, errors can cascade.
IF downstream jobs act on dbt-generated metadata without validation, the risk increases.
mitigations: Add a validation step before dagster consumes dbt outputs.
Require schema checks on all upstream artifacts.
Fail closed on missing or malformed dbt metadata.
Have a human review first-run pipeline outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core explicitly touches data warehouse data, while dagster’s profile shows no touched data classes and no residency or retention controls. Because the pair can move warehouse data through dbt-managed workflows without documented matching compliance controls, the safest reading is a medium compliance mismatch rather than none; uncertainty escalates.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes regulated records, the compliance gap becomes material.
IF either agent logs or retains transformed outputs longer than the source policy, mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling before enabling the pair.
Set explicit retention limits for pipeline artifacts.
Restrict regulated datasets to approved environments.
Document residency and deletion responsibilities.
requires-engineering: align logging and retention controls across both systems.
